Identities:
# Identities
## What the theme covers
Identities explores the nature of the self and what it is to be human. Recommended topics are lifestyles, health and well-being, beliefs and values, subcultures, and language and identity. A guiding question is: what constitutes our identity, and how do we express who we are?

## Useful language
To describe yourself, use je suis, je me considère comme and ce qui me définit, c'est…. To give opinions, use à mon avis, selon moi and je trouve que. Talk about habits with the present tense and about change with the passé composé and imparfait: avant, je mangeais mal, mais maintenant je fais attention.

## Ideas to discuss
Link identity to the francophone world: bilingualism in Québec, regional languages such as Breton and Occitan, and multicultural identity in France. Think about how social media shapes self-image.

## Key terms
le mode de vie: lifestyle, way of life
la santé: health, being healthy
le bien-être: well-being, welfare
les valeurs: values, principles
la croyance: belief, faith
une sous-culture: a subculture
appartenir à: to belong to
le patrimoine: heritage, inherited culture
Experiences:
# Experiences
## What the theme covers
Experiences explores the events that shape our lives. Recommended topics are leisure activities, holidays and travel, life stories, rites of passage, customs and traditions, and migration. A guiding question is: how do our experiences shape us?

## Useful language
Narrate the past with the passé composé for completed actions and the imparfait for background and habits: quand j'étais petit, nous allions à la mer chaque été. Use the plus-que-parfait for an earlier past: j'avais déjà visité Paris. Use the future and conditional for plans: l'année prochaine, je voyagerai; si j'avais de l'argent, je partirais.

## Ideas to discuss
Francophone festivals such as Mardi gras in Louisiana or the Fête de la musique; the gap year; migration to France from North and West Africa.

## Key terms
les loisirs: leisure activities
le voyage: the journey, travel
un rite de passage: a rite of passage
la coutume: custom, tradition
la migration: migration, moving country
un souvenir: a memory, a souvenir
une année sabbatique: a gap year
Human ingenuity:
# Human ingenuity
## What the theme covers
Human ingenuity explores how human creativity and innovation affect our world. Recommended topics are entertainment, artistic expressions, communication and media, technology, and scientific innovation. A guiding question is: how do inventions change the way we live?

## Useful language
Weigh pros and cons with d'un côté… de l'autre, l'avantage, c'est que and l'inconvénient, c'est que. Use the subjunctive after expressions of necessity and doubt: il faut que nous soyons prudents; je doute que la technologie puisse tout résoudre. Use connectives such as cependant, pourtant, en revanche and par conséquent.

## Ideas to discuss
Screen time and social media, artificial intelligence, French cinema and the exception culturelle, French inventions such as the Minitel and the TGV.

## Key terms
les réseaux sociaux: social media
l’intelligence artificielle: artificial intelligence
une invention: an invention
les médias: the media
le divertissement: entertainment, amusement
une découverte: a discovery
cependant: however, nevertheless
Social organization:
# Social organization
## What the theme covers
Social organization explores how groups of people organize themselves. Recommended topics are social relationships, community, social engagement, education, the working world, and law and order. A guiding question is: what is the individual's role in the community?

## Useful language
Use relative pronouns to build complex sentences: qui, que, dont, où and lequel. Express obligation with devoir and il est nécessaire de. Make suggestions with on devrait and il vaudrait mieux. Use impersonal phrases such as il est important que + subjunctive.

## Ideas to discuss
The French school system (le collège, le lycée, le bac), volunteering (le bénévolat), the 35-hour working week, strikes (la grève) and protest movements such as the gilets jaunes.

## Key terms
la communauté: the community
le bénévolat: volunteering, unpaid work
l’enseignement: education, teaching
le monde du travail: the working world
le chômage: unemployment, being out of work
la grève: a strike, industrial action
la loi: the law
Sharing the planet:
# Sharing the planet
## What the theme covers
Sharing the planet explores the challenges and opportunities faced by individuals and communities. Recommended topics are the environment, human rights, peace and conflict, equality, globalization, ethics, and urban and rural environment. A guiding question is: what can we do to protect the planet and each other?

## Useful language
Persuade with il faut absolument, nous devons and il est urgent de. Use the conditional for hypotheses: si tout le monde recyclait, il y aurait moins de déchets. Use the passive voice for processes: les forêts sont détruites.

## Ideas to discuss
Climate change and la COP21 in Paris, recycling, fast fashion, inequality in la Francophonie, the right to education, and life in the banlieue compared with the countryside.

## Key terms
l’environnement: the environment
le réchauffement climatique: global warming
les déchets: waste, rubbish
recycler: to recycle
les droits de l’homme: human rights
la mondialisation: globalization, global integration
l’égalité: equality, being equal
durable: sustainable, long-lasting
Paper 1: writing:
# Paper 1: writing
## The paper
Paper 1 is a writing paper. You choose one of three tasks and write a text of the type asked for: at SL 250–400 words in 1 hour 15 minutes, at HL 450–600 words in 1 hour 30 minutes. It is marked on language, message and conceptual understanding.

## Text types
Text types include the article, blog, email, letter, speech, diary entry, review, interview, brochure, report and proposal. Each text type has conventions: a letter has a date, greeting and sign-off; a blog has a title, date and a chatty tone; a speech addresses the audience directly. Match the register to the audience: use tu with friends and vous for formal writing.

## Tips
Plan the purpose, audience and context first. Use a range of tenses, connectives and idioms. Check agreements, accents and verb endings.

## Key terms
le registre: register, the level of formality
le destinataire: the recipient, the audience
le type de texte: the text type
une formule de politesse: a polite closing formula
Madame, Monsieur: formal letter greeting
Paper 2: listening and reading:
# Paper 2: listening and reading
## The paper
Paper 2 tests receptive skills. The listening section uses three audio texts; the reading section uses three written texts. Questions include multiple choice, true or false with justification, gap-filling, matching and short answers.

## Strategies
Read the questions before you listen or read. Look for synonyms and paraphrases, not identical words. In true/false questions, the justification must be the exact words from the text. Watch for negatives such as ne… jamais, ne… plus and ne… que (only), which change the meaning.

## Key terms
vrai ou faux: true or false
justifiez: justify, give evidence
un synonyme: a synonym
ne… que: only, nothing but
ne… plus: no longer
Individual oral:
# Individual oral
## The assessment
The individual oral is the internal assessment. At SL you describe and discuss a visual stimulus linked to a theme; at HL you discuss an extract from one of the literary works you studied. It includes a presentation of up to 4 minutes, a follow-up discussion, and a general conversation on at least one other theme.

## How to do well
Link the stimulus to the theme and to the francophone world. Use a wide range of vocabulary and structures, and answer with developed opinions rather than short replies. Use fillers such as bon, alors and en fait naturally, and ask for clarification if needed: pourriez-vous répéter ?

## Key terms
une image: an image, a visual stimulus
décrire: to describe
au premier plan: in the foreground
à l’arrière-plan: in the background
pourriez-vous répéter ?: could you repeat?
Literary works:
# Literary works
## Literature at HL
HL students study two literary works in French. Literature helps you explore the themes in depth and builds vocabulary and cultural understanding. The HL individual oral discusses an extract from one of these works.

## Talking about literature
Discuss the plot (l'intrigue), the characters (les personnages), the narrator (le narrateur), the setting, the themes and the author's style. Use the present tense to describe events in a story. Support points with brief quotations and explain their effect. Popular works include Le Petit Prince by Saint-Exupéry, L'Étranger by Camus and Kiffe kiffe demain by Faïza Guène.

## Key terms
l’intrigue: the plot
le personnage: the character
le narrateur: the narrator
l’auteur: the author
un extrait: an extract
le thème: the theme
